author: WP12
summary: Alpha.1-era chapter on the XNB envelope: header, four-valued compression, LZX state, the reader table and name parser, limits and the length cross-check. Stale at TARGET where it calls LZ4 a deliberate refusal and presents the both-directions length rule as general. The site's XNB guide, Tutorial 147 and the runtime internals held the header, limits and maxFileSize caveat; the LZX framing and oracle, name-parser details, per-limit enforcement sites and the run-time versus build-time length rules now live on a new deep dive.

concepts.text: An XNB is a framing header, an optionally decompressed object stream and then the reader architecture; container, reader table and object graph are separate boundaries, and passing one does not establish the next.
tokens: Three boundaries, checked in order
Passing one boundary proves nothing about the next

concepts.text: Header layout: bytes 0-2 magic XNB, byte 3 platform, byte 4 version, byte 5 flags, bytes 6-9 little-endian signed 32-bit total length.
tokens: Total length
One of 16 values

concepts.text: The magic is read one byte at a time through BinaryReader, a deliberate deviation from FNA's four-byte read-then-compare, so a truncated file throws EndOfStreamException at the missing byte.
tokens: A deliberate deviation from FNA
XnbHeaderTest.TruncatedHeaderThrowsEndOfStreamException

concepts.text: Accepted platform bytes are FNA's sixteen: w x m i a d X W n u p M r P g l; identifiers MonoGame added after the fork are refused, so compatibility means the historical FNA/XNA set.
tokens: w x m i a d X W n u p M r P g l
MonoGameWebAssemblyPlatformIsNotAcceptedMatchingFnaExactly

concepts.text: Only versions 4 and 5 are accepted.
tokens: 4 or 5

concepts.text: Flag bits other than the two compression bits, including the HiDef profile bit 0x01, are not interpreted by the reader; the platform byte is kept and acted on only by the SoundEffect reader.
tokens: The graphics-profile bit 0x01 is not acted on by the reader
only the SoundEffect reader acts on it

concepts.text: Compression is a four-valued enum: neither bit None (object stream at byte 10), 0x80 LZX, 0x40 LZ4, both bits Unknown and refused rather than guessing which codec wins.
tokens: Compression is four-valued
Refused rather than guessing which codec wins

concepts.text: Claim that the LZ4 flag is a named ContentLoadException, deliberately deferred: at the snapshot the typed Load<T> path decodes MonoGame's single raw LZ4 block with an in-tree bounded decoder; only the untyped external-reference path still refuses LZ4.
tokens: a header with both bits set is refused
LZ4 is one bounded raw block
concepts.note: Bible (alpha.1-era text) said LZ4 was refused; TARGET decodes it on the typed path.

concepts.text: Both bit values were confirmed against MonoGame's ContentManager.cs; LZX is the historical XNA route and LZ4 MonoGame's, and the enum keeps that provenance explicit instead of treating compression as one Boolean.
tokens: Both bit values were taken from MonoGame's own

concepts.text: CNA's LZX decoder is a line-by-line C++ port of FNA's LzxDecoder.cs (itself from libmspack), keeping FNA's names, control flow and return codes for verification against the original.
tokens: line-by-line C++ port of FNA's

concepts.text: One decoder instance serves one file so the sliding window, repeated-offset LRU and Huffman tables persist across framed blocks; a fresh decoder per block would pass trivial payloads and corrupt real multi-block streams.
tokens: constructs one decoder per file
corrupt real multi-block streams

concepts.text: The window exponent is bounded to 15-21 (UnsupportedLzxWindowSizeRange otherwise) and XNB uses 16.
tokens: UnsupportedLzxWindowSizeRange

concepts.text: Block framing: a two-byte big-endian compressed size per 32 KiB frame, a 0xFF sentinel selecting the five-byte form with an explicit frame size; a zero block or frame size ends the loop.
tokens: a leading 0xFF selects the five-byte form

concepts.text: After all blocks the produced byte count must equal the declared decompressed size exactly; by reading, the comparison happens once after the loop, which does not stop early when output passes the declared size.
tokens: that comparison happens once, after the loop
concepts.note: The late comparison is established by reading, not exercised.

concepts.text: Intel E8 call translation is reproduced unfinished from FNA, so a stream that enables it fails to decode as it would under FNA.
tokens: Intel E8 call translation is reproduced from FNA unfinished

concepts.text: The strongest decoder oracle is cross-implementation: output is compared byte for byte with FNA's unmodified decoder run under Mono on a single-block (Explosion.xnb) and a multi-block (FontCalibri14.xnb, 44,032 bytes) payload.
tokens: LzxDecoderDifferentialTests.cpp
44,032 bytes

concepts.text: The Mono oracle is credited with finding a heap-buffer-overflow in the long-code decode-table growth path, a defect class self-consistency fixtures could miss.
concepts.note: History of a fixed decoder defect from the Bible's source audit; no TARGET record names it, so only the oracle's current role is documented.

concepts.section: The reader table starts inside the decoded stream
concepts.text: The object stream begins with a 7-bit-encoded reader count followed by reader-name and Int32 version pairs; the count is bounded (4,096) and each entry keeps its raw and normalised name.
tokens: keeps both the raw name and its normalised canonical key

concepts.section: The reader table starts inside the decoded stream
concepts.text: Parser errors from the name parser (std::invalid_argument) are rethrown as ContentLoadException at the table boundary, so callers need one exception type for a malformed table.
tokens: a caller needs one exception type for a malformed table

concepts.text: A reader name may contain nested generic arguments, assembly qualifiers, version, culture and public-key tokens, so splitting at the first comma is wrong.
tokens: cutting at the first comma breaks every generic name

concepts.text: The recursive parser tracks bracket depth, strips assembly metadata and rebuilds a canonical Base[[arg1],[arg2]] key; array rank specifiers are kept verbatim after the argument list.
tokens: Base[[arg1],[arg2]]
Array rank specifiers

concepts.text: Type-name recursion is bounded by maxObjectNestingDepth; before the guard a sub-megabyte crafted name could exhaust the C++ stack.
tokens: NestingDepthExceedingDefaultLimitThrowsInvalidArgumentNotCrash

concepts.text: Default limits: maxFileSize 64 MiB, maxDecompressedSize 256 MiB, maxStringBytes 1 MiB, maxTypeReaderCount 4,096, maxObjectNestingDepth 256, maxSharedResourceCount 1,000,000 (plus maxCollectionElementCount 10,000,000).
tokens: maxCollectionElementCount 10,000,000
Object nesting depth

concepts.text: maxFileSize bounds the compressed payload before decompression allocation, not the initial whole-file read: LoadXnbAsset and the manifest scan read the entire file first, so an uncompressed file between 64 MiB and 2 GiB is not refused at run time.
tokens: an uncompressed .xnb between 64 MiB and 2 GiB is not refused by the file-size limit at run time

concepts.text: maxDecompressedSize applies to the size hint and to decoded output, maxStringBytes to reader-table names after the read, maxTypeReaderCount to the table count, maxObjectNestingDepth to type names and object recursion, maxSharedResourceCount to the shared table.
tokens: Limits and where each is enforced

concepts.text: The build-time importer is the route where maxFileSize is a real admission check: a .xnb read as a cna-content source above 64 MiB is refused before reading.
tokens: the file must not exceed 64 MiB

concepts.section: Length checks close the container boundary
concepts.text: The loader cross-checks the declared totalLength against the bytes actually read before using offsets: at least 10, no larger than the file, and at least 14 for a compressed file; uncompressed content starts at byte 10, LZX/LZ4 payload at 14 after the four-byte size.
tokens: requires 14 bytes before a compressed payload

concepts.section: Length checks close the container boundary
concepts.text: Truncation, impossible lengths, unsupported compression and decoded-size disagreement all fail before object readers receive the stream.
tokens: The length cross-check

concepts.section: Length checks close the container boundary
concepts.text: The rule to validate the length relationship in both directions is applied only by the build-time importer (declared length must equal the file size); the run-time check is one-directional, tolerating bytes beyond the declared length.
tokens: checked in one direction only
the declared length must equal the file size exactly
concepts.note: Bible stated the both-directions rule generally; at TARGET only the canonical build-time read enforces equality.

concepts.section: Length checks close the container boundary
concepts.text: The cross-check exists because a file claiming more bytes than it holds would let the LZX branch compute a compressed size that reads past the end of the buffer.
tokens: reads past the end of the buffer

concepts.section: What the container does not prove
concepts.text: A clean container proves only that envelope, compression and reader table are acceptable; reader versions, nested indices, shared-resource fixups, texture level sizes and referenced paths are checked later by the session and the concrete readers.
tokens: a later layer still has to validate what an earlier one accepted

figures.note: Redrawn as a text diagram with the TARGET limits at each layer (LZ4 added, depth and collection limits placed where they are enforced).

issues.text: XnbReadLimits::maxFileSize does not bound the run-time whole-file read (TryReadAssetBytes accepts up to INT32_MAX; ScanXnbReaderNames reads any size).
LZX decode compares the produced length with the declared size only after the last block; output is not capped while decoding.
